paragraphs.text: Black-red ( or BR ), also called Rakdos , is an allied color pair. Black ( ) and red ( ) share a philosophy of individualism; they are the mutual enemies of white ( ), the color of structure and morality. Black and red have more mechanical overlap than most color pairs: they are the best colors at creature removal ; they can both directly attack a player's life total; they share the evergreen keywords menace , haste , flying , and ward for life ; and they have strong sacrifice themes. The black-red color pair lends itself to removal-heavy aggro decks with controlling, tempo elements.

Black seeks power, while red wants to follow its heart. They are mutual enemies of white , the color of collective welfare. Accordingly, black and red's alliance is about individualism. Both colors want to fulfill their own desires, with little regard for rules or authority.

Black-red is the most self-centered color pair; it will stop at nothing to fulfill its immediate desires. Self-assured and decisive, black-red is utterly focused on its current goal, although that goal isn't always consistent. It has an arsenal of tools to kill or destroy whatever gets in its way. Black-red is good at making spontaneous decisions, which can make it an unpredictable opponent, but it's not good at long-term thinking; spontaneous solutions can create more problems down the line, and black-red lacks any sense of discipline or self-restraint.

Black-red is willing to do anything in pursuit of its desires, no matter what rules it breaks or boundaries it pushes. It can be so self-centered that it doesn't understand or care about other people. It rarely experiences regret or remorse. At the same time, black-red also has a vivacious, fun-loving side.

Black and red's disagreements mirror the blue-green conflict of nurture versus nature . Black, an ally of blue , believes that people should forge their own destinies. Red, an ally of green , believes that people should follow their innate desires. Black is also more ambitious and consistent in its goals, whereas red's attention span can be fleeting. And red, unlike black, is willing to act selflessly for its loved ones.
Examples of Black-red heroes include Angrath and Xantcha , while villains include Rakdos and Tibalt .

Black and red have the most mechanical overlap of any color pair except green-white . Differences between the two colors have been deliberately carved out to keep them from feeling too similar. Black has relatively higher toughness than red, and it causes life loss instead of dealing damage . Red used to have "This creature attacks each turn if able" to contrast with black's "This creature can't block", but the latter played better, so now both colors use it.

Black and red are the best colors at killing creatures . Black-red decks tend to be aggressive , but not as aggressive as red-white; the abundance of creature removal means they play more of a tempo game, keeping the board clear of blockers for long enough to get their own creatures through.
The following mechanics are shared by black and red.
These multicolored cards best exemplify the strengths of black and red:
Blightning — Black's discard ability combined with red's direct damage
Sarkhan the Mad — Black's "greatness at any cost" combined with red's direct damage
Malfegor — High-powered dragon combined with red and black's tandem field wipe
Deathbringer Thoctar — Red's growth and damage-dealing capabilities teamed up with black's death motif
